finding.claim: /fetch2 forwards an attacker-supplied URL to requests.get after only checking the scheme, allowing requests to internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints, with the response body returned to the caller.

trace.note: is_http_url(url) called as the only gate
is_http_url returns urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no hostname or IP check
requests.get(url, timeout=5) with default redirect following; response.text[:200] returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (http/https) only. No hostname allowlist, no IP/private-range check, no port restriction, redirects followed by default, no DNS pinning.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on /fetch2 is is_http_url at views.py:20, which validators.py:7 implements as a scheme-only test (urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https")). The hostname/IP screen is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2. requests.get at views.py:22 uses default allow_redirects=True.
verdict.reason: The URL comes unauthenticated from request.args at views.py:19, the only gate at views.py:20 is the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7), and views.py:22 fetches it with redirects enabled and returns text[:200] to the caller, so internal, loopback, and metadata addresses are reachable.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the hostname's resolved addresses with is_safe_url, then fetches the URL by name, which re-resolves DNS; an attacker-controlled name with near-zero TTL can rebind from a public address to an internal one between check and use.

trace.note: urlparse(url); requires scheme http/https and non-empty hostname
socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port) — first DNS resolution; all returned addresses checked
requests.get(url) performs a second, independent DNS resolution inside urllib3; no IP pinning between check and connect

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist; hostname presence; resolve-then-check over all getaddrinfo results against private/loopback/link-local/reserved; allow_redirects=False blocks redirect-based bypass. Not guarded: TOCTOU between check-time and connect-time resolution. Exploitation requires attacker control of DNS for the supplied name.

verdict.guard_found: validators.py:12-17 (scheme check plus resolve-then-reject private/loopback/link-local/reserved addresses via getaddrinfo). This is not an exact hostname membership, anchored match, or scheme-plus-host-allowlist guard, so it does not close the finding. views.py:14 re-resolves the name inside requests.get with no IP pinning. allow_redirects=False at views.py:14 only blocks redirect bypass, not rebinding.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `url` from request.args (views.py:11) passes is_safe_url (views.py:12, validators.py:14-17), which resolves DNS once, then requests.get at views.py:14 resolves the same hostname again with no IP pinning, so a low-TTL attacker-controlled name can rebind between check and connect. The response body is returned (views.py:14, first 200 chars), so the impact is readable SSRF.
